question: Can photography and OCR of a displayed document be defeated, given the page must be legible to its reader?
answer: Partly. Temporal decomposition raises cost but is not secure, and the reason is structural. Aperture bounding is secure per capture, because it removes the information rather than obscuring it.

asymmetries_considered.verdict: rejected without experiment — degrades the page for the human at least as much, and vision models keep improving; prior art has lost repeatedly

asymmetries_considered.idea: Spectral metamerism (inks or subpixels metameric to cones but not to a camera CFA)
asymmetries_considered.verdict: real and used in security printing, but needs controlled media or hardware; out of scope for a software tool

asymmetries_considered.idea: Temporal complementary decomposition (page = time-average of frames)
Aperture / foveal bounding (only a small window ever carries true text)
asymmetries_considered.verdict: BUILT AND MEASURED — the only construction here that is not defeatable by image processing

temporal_decomposition.construction: two frames F1 = LT + d, F2 = LT - d with a zero-mean mask d; the eye integrates the average, which is exactly LT; a screenshot captures one frame
temporal_decomposition.range_constraint: content confined to luminance [1/3, 2/3] so |d| <= 1/3 and no clipping; the average is then exact, not approximate

attempt_1_decoy_overlay.verdict: FAILED — overlaying a second document adds a layer of opposite polarity rather than destroying glyph structure; OCR reads straight through it, and the factor of two amplifies the true signal in the compensator

attempt_2_block_mask.verdict: BROKEN — a piecewise-constant mask lives in each cell's DC term; the cell median estimates it robustly because glyph ink is a minority of any cell. The grid is recoverable by brute force over ~256 (size, offset) pairs, each scored by whether OCR returns English.

attempt_3_dense_text_mask.verdict: BROKEN — near-binary content plus near-binary mask sums to four distinguishable levels and the map back to ink/background is injective

temporal_decomposition.sparse_text_mask_note: a mask made of ordinary decoy text covers only ~4% of the page, so it hides almost nothing (leaked 0.28 raw)
temporal_decomposition.why_no_variant_works: Mask amplitude is bounded by display headroom, and headroom trades directly against the content contrast the reader needs. At any human-readable contrast the per-frame signal-to-mask ratio is about 1, and OCR beats that by aggregating over the many pixels of a glyph. Lowering content contrast to widen the mask lowers it for the human too, because the human sees the average.
temporal_decomposition.what_it_is_still_good_for: off-the-shelf OCR on a single captured frame recovers nothing (0.000-0.053). It defeats the casual screenshot on every platform with no help from the operating system, which matters because capture exclusion is unavailable on bare X11 and in a web viewer. It is cost, not security.

aperture_bounding.construction: only a small window carries the true text; the rest of the frame carries decoy text
aperture_bounding.critical_detail: the out-of-aperture region must carry DIFFERENT information, not attenuated true text. Attenuating contrast by 12x still lost the whole page (recovery 1.000) because ordinary autocontrast restores it.
aperture_bounding.why_this_one_holds: the true text is absent from the frame outside the aperture, so no amount of image processing extracts it. The bound is on information content, not on perception.
aperture_bounding.human_cost: unmeasured. Peripheral acuity is poor enough that a reader cannot read outside roughly 2 degrees anyway, which is why this is plausible, but that is an argument and not a user study.

what_remains_open: Video recording defeats both. Aperture bounding converts one screenshot into recording an entire reading session, which is a different and more deliberate act, but it is not prevention.
Flicker is a seizure and migraine trigger. Any frame-alternating display needs a warning, an opt-out and an alternative route, and comfortable operation needs 240 Hz hardware.
The 2:1 contrast ratio the temporal construction requires is a real accessibility cost borne by the reader.
Printed pages are untouched by any of this; the print path keeps only the chaff decoy and the kerning fingerprint.
